title: Macaroni Cheese
subtitle: Pasta in a rich cheddar sauce, baked until golden
excerpt: Macaroni cheese is pasta cooked in a thick, creamy cheese sauce and baked with a crispy top. The sauce is a simple white sauce loaded with cheddar and a little mustard. This is a proper, filling dinner.
sourceNotes: Macaroni cheese appears in early British and American cookbooks from the 18th century. It became a popular British staple through school dinners and home cooking across the 20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble unbaked up to 24 hours ahead. Add 5 minutes to the baking time if going in from cold.

content.text: Cook the pasta until just underdone. It will continue cooking in the oven and you do not want it to go soft. The sauce should taste well-seasoned before you mix them together.

items.prepNote: grated: 200g into the sauce, 50g for the top

content.text: Cook the pasta in a large pan of salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain and set aside.
Melt the butter in the saucepan over a medium heat. Add the flour and stir together for 1 minute.
Pour in the milk slowly, whisking all the time. Add it in a thin stream to avoid lumps.
Keep stirring over a medium heat until the sauce thickens. About 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in 200g of the cheddar, the mustard, and the nutmeg. Season well with salt and pepper.
Add the pasta to the sauce and stir to coat.
Pour into a large baking dish. Scatter the remaining 50g of cheddar over the top.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden on top.

items.symptom: The sauce has lumps in it.
items.cause: Milk was added too fast or in too large a quantity at once.
items.fix: Whisk vigorously off the heat, then return and cook until smooth.

items.symptom: The pasta is dry and the sauce has been absorbed.
items.cause: Pasta was overcooked before baking, absorbing extra sauce.
items.fix: Stir in a splash of milk before baking to loosen the dish.
